svg.title: Relay Reef Plus Rev 1.0 wiring reference
svg.desc: Wiring reference with neck and middle lipsticks on a two-pole three-way blade, a GFS Vintage 59 bridge humbucker, two 500k audio concentric pots giving each branch a reverse-independent volume and its own tone, branches joined at BUS, operating states, and common ground.

g.text: MATCH IDENTICAL BOXED NET LABELS • FUNCTIONAL SWITCH CONTACTS MUST BE METERED
Use supplied lead guides and a meter; labels show electrical roles, not wire colors
Functional contact map • verify by continuity
Rows are the two poles; columns are the three blade positions (throws 1, 2, 3).
Jumper A1–A2 (NL-H), B2–B3 (ML-H), and the two commons (L-SEL). A3 and B1 stay open.
The blade points toward the lipstick it selects. Position 2 joins both in parallel.
L-SEL goes to the lipstick volume wiper and tone. The humbucker does not pass through this switch.
Each source enters its volume on the WIPER.
CW lug → BUS • CCW lug → GND • clockwise = louder.
Turning one volume down grounds only its own source,
never BUS, so the other branch keeps playing.
Each tone taps its own source before the volume. With
that volume up, the tone also darkens the whole output.
No master volume or tone. No treble bleed.
Two stacked decks of one part
REAR VIEW • shaft away • lugs down • meter which deck each shaft turns
Volume: clockwise = louder. Tone: clockwise = brighter.
Two stacked decks of one part
REAR VIEW • shaft away • lugs down • meter which deck each shaft turns
Volume: clockwise = louder. Tone: clockwise = brighter.
GND = pickup returns + separate shields/cases, both volume CCW lugs,
both tone-cap returns, and the jack sleeve.
Standard practice: pot cases, switch chassis, cavity shielding, and
bridge/string ground join the same ground network.
Humbucker in full series: insulate a single split lead, or join and
insulate two separate series ends. Never ground the series junction.
Meter the blade in all three positions. With one volume at zero,
the other branch must still reach the jack.
